full_judgment:
Abdur Rob J: This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party No.1 to show cause as to why the proceeding of Metro Special Case No. 154 of 2008 corresponding to ACC GR Case No. 22 of2008 arising out of Shahbag PS Case No. 53 dated February 26, 2008 under sections 409/109 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947, now pending in the Court of Metropolitan Senior Special Judge, Dhaka should not be quashed and for such order or further order or orders be passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The prosecution case, briefly, is that Boropukuria Coal Mining Company Ltd. (here- in after referred to as BCMCL) floated international tender for extraction of coal from where three companies known as Shandong Ludi, Suja Coal and, CMC participated in the bid and ultimately as the lowest bidder Shandong Ludi's offer was accepted whereupon BCMCL issued a work order amounting to Taka 335,08,05,382.18 asking Shandong Ludi to execute Bank Guarantee and Performance Guarantee as per terms of tender. But without executing such guarantee the bidder company placed its demand to enhance the agreed price on August 12, 2004 for which BCMCL refused to accept its claim, rather cancelled the work order and accepting the request of CMC Consortium and decided to issue work order in favour of the consortium on the identical terms and conditions as previously issued in favour of Shandong Ludi but CMC consortium also did not accept the same rather requested for further negotiation to enhance the rate already quoted. In such circumstances Chairman, Petro Bangla, in pursuance of the regulations of Boropukuria Coal Mining Company Ltd. (BCMCL), sent a request to the Ministry of Energy for re-tender which was refused and ultimately a committee headed by the then State Minister for Energy Mr AKM Mosharraf Hossain recommended in favour of the execution of the contract with CMC Consortium and placed such proposal to the Cabinet Purchase Committee at the behest of the Ministry of Energy where the accused-petitioner being member of that committee accepted such proposal of the Ministry, ignoring the recommendation for re-tender allowing the Consortium to make pecuniary benefit of to the tune of Taka 158 cores of public money and thereby committed an offence punishable under sections 409/406/109/419/420 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947. 

 3. Thereafter, Anti-Corruption Commission took up the matter for inquiry and ultimately lodged the ejahar where one Deputy Director Mr Monirul Haque was entrusted to investigate the case but he submitted a final report with a recommendation to discharge the accused-petitioner along with others with an observation that no prima facie case was found established against them. 

 4. However, on further investigation, the investigating officer Mr Abul Kashem Fakir found prima facie case against the FIR named accused including the petitioner under sections 409/406/109/419/420 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947.andrecommended for their trial for misappropriation of public money by misuse of official power in connivance with each other. Finding portion of charge-sheet reads as follows: 

 7 Mr AJ Mohammad Ali the learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the accused has submitted that the allegation as has been brought against the petitioner in the FIR does neither constitute any offence within the mischief of sections 409/109 nor it constitutes offence under section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 and, as such, the proceedings, so far as the petitioner is concerned is liable to be quashed for ends of justice. 

 8. Mr Ali has further submitted that since FIR does not disclose any offence implicating the accused-petitioner in the criminal proceeding under the code no proceeding can be allowed to continue. Mr Ali has' referred to case of Sheikh Hasina Wazed alias Sheikh Hasina vs State reported in 63 DLR 162 to assail the impugned proceeding on the ground that without proper sanction as required under section 32 of the Anti- Corruption Commission Act, 2004 no proceeding can be allowed to continue. Even any mechanical sanction as available in Annexure A-1 to the petition is not enough to legalize the proceeding against the accused petitioner. Moreover, such mechanical sanction has only been accorded by one of the member of a Commission not by the Commission. Moreover, in no way Anti- Corruption Commission reserves any right to send back the case for further investigation where final report has been submitted by a competent investigating officer appointed by the Commission. 

 9. Mr Ali has also argued that there is nothing within the four comers of the Anti-Corruption Commission Ain, 2004 or in the Rule, 2007 any specific provision to hold any further investigation; but yet it was held with an ulterior motive to rope up the accused petitioner for the purpose of harassment in the name of the trial. Mr Ali has also landed his argument alleging that the offence as narrated in the FIR and police report does not, at all, come within the mischief of "criminal misconduct" as defined in section 5(1)( d) of the Prevention of Corruption Act or any other clause available therein. 

 13. Relying on the decision in the case of Anti-Corruption Commission vs Dr Mohiuddin Khan Alamgir reported in 62 DLR 290 Mr Khan has urged that no sanction is required for lodging an ejahar or 'complaint-petition rather only one sanction is required, to be accorded by the Commission under section 32 of the  দুর্নীতি দমন কমিশন আইন-২০০৪ read with section 15(2) of the দুর্নীতি দমন কমিশন আইন-২০০৭। before taking cognizance of the offence and issuance of the process which has already been complied with. As such question of quashment on such ground does not; at all arise. 

 14. Regarding mechanical sanction Mr Khan has referred to the case of Habibur Rahman Molla vs State reported in 61 DLR 1 which has also been affirmed by the Appellate Division reported in 62 DLR (AD) 233 where it has clearly been observed that under the present Rule where Form No. 3 has been prescribed to accord sanction the question of assigning any reason to show Commission's satisfaction is not required. 

 15. Moreover, against the argument placed by the learned Advocate for the petitioner relating to the power of the Anti-Corruption Commission, so far it relates' to further investigation Mr. Khan has drawn our attention to the provision sections 17 and 19 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Ain, 2004 where the power and the function of the Commission for inquiry or investigation has been clearly spelt out. More so, as he continued it is a settled principle of law that prosecution is always at liberty to cause further investigation to be made if it is required for ends of justice. In the instant case the initial investigating officer, without collecting evidence required by law, simply recommended for discharge on the basis of the statements of the accused persons, recorded under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Commission had no other alternative but' to pass an order for further investigation asking him to unearth facts behind the deal involving huge public money. Anti-Corruption Commission, being a prosecuting agency rightly passed an order of further investigation in a case involving huge public money as has been empowered by sections 19 arid 20 0f the দুর্নীতি দমন কমিশন আইন-২০০৪। In this context sub-section procedure; appears to be the most relevant law, which provides for further investigation when material evidence becomes available afterwards. 

 17. Mr Khan by reference to the pre-emble has submitted 'that ACC in order to carry out the purpose of the Act is competent to take any action incidental or ancillary to investigation including further investigation if the report is found to be biased or otherwise 'incomplete 'or 'defective. Moreover "section 17(এ)(ট) of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 has also. empowered the Commission to perform any function to achieve the objective of the Jaw relating to prevention of corruption .which necessarily includes further investigation within the residuary power given by section 19(1)(Cha) of the Anti-Corruption Commission Ain, 2004. This power of further investigation has also been settled in a case Abdus Salam Master alias Salam vs State reported in 36 DLR (AD) 58. 

 18. Last of in reply to the argument placed by Mr Mohammad Ali Mr Khan submitted that the recital of the FIR and police report clearly reveals a strong prima facie case of "criminal misconduct" as defined in section 5(1)( d) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947. Therefore, the same cannot be decided between affidavit and counter affidavits in exercise power under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 21. In fact, this point has been clearly decided in a case of Habibur Rahman Mollah vs State reported in 61 DLR 1 which has been confirmed by the Appellate Division 'reported in 62 DLR (AD) 233 where their Lordships of the Apex Court have made the following observation:' 

 22. Moreover, in a case of ACC vs Dr Mohiuddin Khan Alamgir reported in 62 DLR (AD) 290 their Lordships of the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court also made the following observation relating to sanction of the prosecution as required under section 32 of the ACC Act read with section 15(2) of the Bidhimala, 2007: 

 23. In the instant case such sanction (Annexure-E) to the petition is available for prosecution. In such circumstances we have no hesitation to reject the contention raised by learned Advocate AJ Mohammad Ali In fact, the sanction as required by law is available in the record. 

 24. Turning to the question of means rea as argued by the learned Advocates for petitioner, we are of the view that in the true nature of things it is hardly possible to prove dishonest intention without trial. Or in other words criminal intention is a mental act of the accused persons which is something to be, unearthed either by circumstantial or oral evidence to be adduced during the course of trial. In the instant case there is at least a clear and strong prima facie case of dishonest misappropriation of public property or otherwise disposal of public property in violation of law constituting offence punishable u/s 409/109 read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947. 

 25. Our view lends support from the Miscellaneous Case Nos. 8394 of 2009 filed by Md Nazrul Islam vs Anti-Corruption Commission, and 8393 of 2009 filed by Moazzem Hossain vs Anti-Corruption Commission, wherein the proceeding of the instant case was challenged on similar ground and Rules were issued and upon final hearing all the. Rules were discharged. 

 27. In the result; this Rule is discharged. The order of stay granted earlier is hereby vacated. The trial court is directed to proceed with the case in accordance with law.
